# Nimbus Notes — Website assessment — 8 September 2026

## What this is

- Nimbus Notes is a notes app that keeps notes on the device first and syncs them across a person's devices. It works offline, exports to a folder of Markdown files, and stores data in the EU (Frankfurt) by default.
- An eight-person company founded in 2023 by Priya Raman, based in Bristol. It has three plans: Starter ("For individuals."), Team ("For growing teams.") and Enterprise. Every plan says "Contact sales" and none shows a price.

## How it was produced

- Two simulated visitors went through the live marketing site in a real browser, and every step was recorded. One evaluated it for a team on a desktop (1440×900, 6½ minutes). The other was a sceptical visitor on an iPhone 13 (about 3 minutes).
- Both visitors were constructed personas, not real customers. A separate reviewer scored the recording afterwards, using only what the recording showed.

## Contents

## Objectives

## Top 5 — fix these first

Neither visitor could tell from the site what Nimbus Notes is or who it is for, and the one button that offers to show the product does nothing.

| # | Severity | What is happening | What it costs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 | **Landing fold never says what the product is; both personas guessed 'notes' from the name** (`0e2fadb02a78`). The screen shows "Your thoughts, everywhere.", a purple blob and a jargon subhead | Neither visitor ever understood the product. Both left with a guess based on the name | Copy change |
| 2 | P1 | **The only 'See it in action' button goes nowhere, so nothing on the site ever shows the product** (`e145f210ba5e`). The link has no destination | Both visitors clicked it, nothing happened, and they left without seeing the product. That includes the sceptic, who had come to see it "remember" something | Design change |

- Only two findings are serious enough for this list. The other six are minor friction or polish, and they are in the full report.
- Effort: #1 is a copy rewrite of the hero. #2 needs something real to link to, such as a screenshot, a short video or a tour section, plus a change to the button's design.

## What a buyer could and could not establish

| Question the buyer had | Answer from the site |
|---|---|
| What is it? | **Not answered.** Both visitors guessed "notes" from the name, at 00:06 and 00:08. No time to understanding was recorded for either |
| Who is it for? | **Not answered on the home page.** The audience is stated only on the Pricing cards. The evaluator still had this question open at 06:30 |
| What does it cost? | **Not found.** The evaluator opened Pricing at 01:48 and found three plans, all "Contact sales". They gave up at 02:30 after 2 pages |
| Who is behind it? | **Yes, on About.** Named founder, Bristol, company number, eight people. The sceptic found this at 01:30 and the evaluator at 03:50 |
| Where is my data stored? | **Yes, but on About, not Privacy.** "In the EU (Frankfurt) by default". The sceptic found this at 01:50 |
| What does "remembers everything" look like? | **Not shown.** The "See it in action" button is dead |

## In their own words

| Who | When | What they said | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| evaluator | 00:06 | "Some kind of notes app, from the name. The headline doesn't say." | session.log:6 · Top 5 #1 |
| sceptic | 00:08 | "What is it? Notes, I think. For who? Doesn't say." | session.log:6 · Top 5 #1 |
| evaluator | 00:18 | "I don't know what either of those means. I'll assume it syncs." | session.log:10 |
| evaluator | 00:40 | "Clicked "See it in action". Nothing happened. The page didn't move. Clicked again. Still nothing." | session.log:12 · 00-landing.png · Top 5 #2 |
| sceptic | 02:20 | "I want to see it "remember" something. The button does nothing when I tap it." | session.log:13 · Top 5 #2 |
| sceptic | 01:30 | "Priya Raman, Bristol, 2023, company number 14482201, eight people. Good. That is a real company." | session.log:11 · 02-about.png |
| evaluator | 04:20 | "The About page has questions and answers — works offline, can export, data in Frankfurt. Those are actual answers. Why isn't this on the home page?" | session.log:25 · 05-about.png |
| evaluator | debrief Q6 | "Close but off — the line is on the page, but nothing shows me it happening, and the page around it is about vaults and graphs." | persona-debrief.md Q6 |

- Both speakers were constructed personas, not customers.

## What the site does well

- The About page reads like a real business: a named founder, an address, a company number and a team size. Both visitors said this was where they began to believe the company exists.
- The About FAQ gives concrete answers: it works offline, it exports to Markdown, and data is stored in Frankfurt. The evaluator called these "actual answers".
- The Pricing cards state the audience in plain words: "For individuals." / "For growing teams."
- The promise that brought the evaluator to the site ("Nimbus remembers everything so you never start from zero") appears in the "How it works" section of the home page.

## What each check looked for

| Check | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| **Clarity** | Can a visitor say what this is, who it is for, and what to do next? |

## How each area scores

## How to read these findings

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🔴 **P0** | Blocks the job, or breaks trust badly enough that people leave |
| 🟠 **P1** | They get through, but would not become a customer |
| 🟡 **P2** | Noticeable friction; erodes value over time |
| ⚪ **P3** | Polish. Worth fixing, changes nothing on its own |

- When several checks independently find the same problem, that agreement is strong evidence. Only one check ran here, so no finding has that kind of confirmation.
- Every finding is in the full report, with screenshots, log lines and steps to reproduce.

## Limits of this assessment

- **Only Clarity was scored.** The run also planned checks for Conversion, Trust and credibility, Performance and delivery, Search visibility and Answer-engine readiness. None of them is in this report. The missing prices, the seven-field demo form, the contradiction between the cookie bar and the privacy page, and the anonymous testimonials were all seen during the visits but have not been scored.
- **The visitors were constructed.** They were generic personas, not interviewed customers, and their sessions were hand-authored rather than recorded live.
- **Coverage was standard depth, with no auditor follow-up.** The test used two devices: a 1440×900 desktop and an iPhone 13.
- **Some surfaces were never seen.** The Features page returned a 404 error. The desktop screenshot below the fold came out blank, so the sections below the fold are known only from the written log. The mobile visitor never opened Pricing.
- **There are no speed or performance numbers here.** They belong to the Performance and delivery check, which was not scored.
